q: If A and B together can complete a piece of work in 15 days and B alone in 20 days, in how many days can A alone complete the work?
s: 1 st method: A and B complete a work in = 15 days One day's work of (A + B) = $$\frac{1}{{15}}$$ B complete the work in = 20 days; One day's work of B = $$\frac{1}{{20}}$$ Then, A's one day's work $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{{15}} - \frac{1}{{20}} \\ & = \frac{{4 - 3}}{6} \\ & = \frac{1}{{60}} \end{aligned}$$ Thus, A can complete the work in = 60 days. 2 nd method: (A + B)'s one day's % work = $$\frac{{100}}{{15}}$$ = 6.66% B's one day's % work = $$\frac{{100}}{{20}}$$ = 5% A's one day's % work = 6.66 - 5 = 1.66% Thus, A need = $$\frac{{100}}{{1.66}}$$ = 60 days to complete the work.

q: If A and B together can complete a work in 18 days, A and C together in 12 days, and B and C together in 9 days, then B alone can do the work in:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{One}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{of}} \\ & \left( {A + B} \right) = \frac{1}{{18}}\,.......(1) \\ & {\text{One}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{of}} \\ & \left( {A + C} \right) = \frac{1}{{12}}\,.......\left( 2 \right) \\ & {\text{One}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{of}} \\ & \left( {B + C} \right) = \frac{1}{9}\,.......\left( 3 \right) \\ & {\text{Adding}}\,\left( {\text{1}} \right){\text{,}}\,\left( {\text{2}} \right)\,{\text{and}}\,\left( {\text{3}} \right) \\ & 2 \times \left( {A + B + C} \right) = { {\frac{1}{{18}}} + {\frac{1}{{12}}} + {\frac{1}{9}} } \\ & 2(A + B + C) = \frac{1}{4} \\ & {\text{One day's work of}} \\ & {A + B + C} = \frac{1}{8} \\ & B = {\frac{1}{8}} - \left( {A + C} \right) \\ & B = {\frac{1}{8}} - {\frac{1}{{12}}} \\ & {\text{One day's work of}} \\ & B = \frac{{ {3 - 2} }}{{24}} = \frac{1}{{24}} \\ & B\,{\text{need}}\,24\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A and B together can complete a work in 3 days. They start together but after 2 days, B left the work. If the work is completed after two more days, B alone could do the work in
s: 1 st Method: (A+B)'s one day's work = $$\frac{1}{3}$$ part (A+B) works 2 days together = $$\frac{2}{3}$$ part Remaining work = $$1 - \frac{2}{3}$$ = $$\frac{1}{3}$$ part $$\frac{1}{3}$$ part of work is completed by A in two days Hence, one day's work of A = $$\frac{1}{6}$$ Then, one day's work of B = $$\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{6}$$ = $$\frac{1}{6}$$ So, B alone can complete the whole work in 6 days. 2 nd Method: (A+B)'s one day's % work = $$\frac{{100}}{3}$$ = 33.3% Work completed in 2 days = 66.6% Remaining work = 33.4% One day's % work of A = $$\frac{{33.4}}{2}$$ = 16.7% One day's work of B = 33.4 - 16.7 = 16.7% B alone can complete the work in, = $$\frac{{100}}{{16.7}}$$ = 5.98 days ≈ 6 days.

q: A can complete a piece of work in 18 days, B in 20 days and C in 30 days, B and C together start the work and forced to leave after 2 days. The time taken by A alone to complete the remaining work is:
s: 1 st Method: $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {B + C} \right)\,2\,{\text{days}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = 2 \times \left( {\frac{1}{{20}} + \frac{1}{{30}}} \right) \\ & = 2 \times {\frac{{3 + 2}}{{60}}} \\ & = \frac{1}{6}{\text{part}} \\ & {\text{Remaining}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = 1 - \frac{1}{6} \\ & = \frac{5}{6}\text{part} \\ & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{one}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = \frac{1}{{18}}{\text{part}} \\ & {\text{Time taken to complete the work}} \\ & = \frac{{ {\frac{5}{6}} }}{{ {\frac{1}{{18}}} }}\,{\text{days}} \\ & {\text{Hence,}} \\ & {\text{Time taken to complete the work}} \\ & = {\frac{5}{6}} \times 18 \\ & = 15\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$ 2 nd Method: % of work B completes in one day = $$\frac{{100}}{{20}}$$ = 5%; % of work C completes in one day = $$\frac{{100}}{{30}}$$ = 3.33%; % of work (A + B) completes together in one day = 5 + 3.33 = 8.33%; % work (A + B) completes together in 2 days = 8.66 × 2 = 16.66%; Remaining work = 100 - 16.66 = 83.34%; % of work A completes in 1 day = $$\frac{{100}}{{18}}$$ = 5.55% Time taken to complete the remaining work by A = $$\frac{{83.34}}{{5.55}}$$ = 15 days

q: Working 5 hours a day, A can Complete a work in 8 days and working 6 hours a day, B can complete the same work in 10 days. Working 8 hours a day, they can jointly complete the work in:
s: 1 st Method: Working 5 hours a day, A can complete the work in 8 days i.e. = 5 × 8 = 40 hours Working 6 hours a day, B can complete the work in 10 days i.e. = 6 × 10 = 60 hours (A + B)'s 1 hour's work, $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{{40}} + \frac{1}{{60}} \\ & = \frac{{3 + 2}}{{120}} \\ & = \frac{5}{{120}} \\ & = \frac{1}{{24}} \end{aligned}$$ Hence, A and B can complete the work in 24 hours i.e. they require 3 days to complete the work. 2 nd Method: % 1 hour's work of A = $$\frac{{100}}{{40}}$$ = 2.5% % 1 hour's work of B = $$\frac{{100}}{{60}}$$ = 1.66% (A + B) one hour's % work, = (2.5 + 1.66) = 4.16% Time to complete the work, = $$\frac{{100}}{{4.16}}$$ = 24 hours Then, $$\frac{{24}}{8}$$ = 3 days They need 3 days, working 8 hours a day to complete the work.

q: Ganga and Saraswati, working separately can mow field in 8 and 12 hours respectively. If they work in stretches of one hour alternately. Ganga is beginning at 9 a.m., when will the moving be completed?
s: According to question, Ganga begins at 9 am and she does 3 units/hours Saraswati begins at 10 am and she does 2 units/hours So by 11 am they complete 5 units Time $$= \frac{{{\text{T}}{\text{.W}}.}}{{3 + 2}} = \frac{{24}}{5}$$ (4 cycle of 2 hrs each + 4 units left) And now ganga will complete 3 unit out of 4 units in 1 hr Now, rest 1 unit work done by = $$\frac{1}{2}$$ hr Total time = 8 + 1 + $$\frac{1}{2}$$ = 9$$\frac{1}{2}$$ hr Hence, Work finished at = 9 am + 9$$\frac{1}{2}$$ hr = 6:30 PM Alternate Solution: Work done by Ganga in 1 hour = $$\frac{1}{8}$$ Work done by Saraswati in 1 hour = $$\frac{1}{12}$$ They are working alternatively with Ganga beginning the job. Work done in every two hours = $$\frac{1}{8}$$ + $$\frac{1}{12}$$ = $$\frac{5}{24}$$ Work done in 4 × 2 = 8 hours = $$\frac{5\times4}{24}$$ = $$\frac{5}{6}$$ Remaining work = 1 - $$\frac{5}{6}$$ = $$\frac{1}{6}$$ In 9th hour, Ganga starts the work and does $$\frac{1}{8}$$ of the work Work remaining = $$\frac{1}{6}$$ - $$\frac{1}{8}$$ = $$\frac{1}{24}$$ In 10th hour, Saraswati starts the work Time needed to finish the remaining work $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{\frac{1}{{24}}}}{{\frac{1}{{12}}}} \\ & = \frac{1}{{24}} \times 12 \end{aligned}$$ $$=$$ 0.5 hours $$=$$ 30 minutes i.e., work will be completed in 9 hour 30 minutes, after 9 AM i.e., at 6:30 PM

q: If 10 men can do a piece of work in 12 days, the time taken by 12 men to do the same piece of work will be:
s: Here, we use work equivalence method; 10 × 12 = 12 × x Or, x = 10 days To understand the work equivalence method, we use a graphic as follows: Men Days 10 ↓ 12 12 ↑ x (let) Here, the two arrows, downward (↓) and upward (↑) show variation between men and days. [If downward arrows show decrements then upward arrows show increments and vice-verse.] Thus, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{10}}{{12}} = \frac{{\text{x}}}{{12}} \\ & {\text{or, x}} = \frac{{10 \times 12}}{{12}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 10\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: To complete a work, A takes 50% more time than B. If together they take 18 days to complete the work, how much time shall B take to do it?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{We have}} \\ & {\text{B}} = \frac{3}{2} \times {\text{A}} \\ & \to {\text{A}} = \frac{2}{3} \times {\text{B}} \\ & {\text{One day's work,}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{A}} + {\text{B}} = \frac{1}{{18}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2}{3} \times {\text{B}} + {\text{B}} = \frac{1}{{18}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{5}{3} \times {\text{B}} = \frac{1}{{18}} \\ & {\text{One}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{B}} \\ & = \frac{3}{{90}} \end{aligned}$$ B alone can complete the work in $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{90}}{3} \\ & = 30\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: If 10 men or 20 boys can make 260 mats in 20 days, then how many mats will be made by 8 men and 4 boys in 20 days?
s: 10 men = 20 boys →1 men = 2 boys 8 men = 2 × 8 boys = 16 boys Then, (16 boys + 4 boys) = 20 boys can make 260 mats in 20 days Now, It can be calculated by work equivalence method: 20 × 260 × 20 = x × 20 × 20 x = 260 mats

q: A complete $$\frac{7}{{10}}$$ of a work in 15 days, then he completed the remaining work with the help of B in 4 days. In how many day A and B can complete entire work together?
s: $$\frac{7}{{10}}$$ part of work has been completed by A in 15 days. Then, Rest work = 1 - $$\frac{7}{{10}}$$ = $$\frac{3}{{10}}$$ part Given, That $$\frac{3}{{10}}$$ part of the work is completed by A and B together in 4 days. Means, (A + B) completed the $$\frac{3}{{10}}$$ of work in 4 days So, (A + B)'s 1 day's work = $$\frac{3}{{10 \times 4}}$$ = $$\frac{3}{{40}}$$ Hence, (A + B) can complete the work in $$\frac{{40}}{3}$$ = $$13\frac{1}{3}$$ days

q: A can complete a piece of work in 36 days, B in 54 days and C in 72 days. All the three began the work the work together but A left 8 days before the completion of the work and B 12 days before the completion of work. Only C worked up to the end. In how many days was the work completed?
s: Let the work be completed in x days. C work for x days then A works for (x - 8) days and B works for (x - 12) days. According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & {\frac{{ {x - 8} }}{{36}} + \frac{{ {x - 12} }}{{54}} + \frac{x}{{72}}} = 1 \\ & {\frac{{ {6x - 48 + 4x - 48 + 3x} }}{{216}}} = 1 \\ & 13x - 96 = 216 \\ & 13x = 216 + 96 = 312 \\ & x = \frac{{312}}{{13}} \\ & x = 24\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: While working 7 hour a day, A alone can complete a piece of work in 6 days and B alone in 8 days. In what time would they complete it together, 8 hour a day?
s: A can complete the work in 7 × 6 = 42 hours 1 hour's work of A = $$\frac{1}{{42}}$$ B can complete the work in 7 × 8 = 56 hours 1 hour's work of B = $$\frac{1}{{56}}$$ (A + B)'s 1 hour's work $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{{42}} + \frac{1}{{56}} \\ & = \frac{{4 + 3}}{{168}} \\ & = \frac{7}{{168}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Time taken by (A + B) working 8 hours daily $$\frac{{168}}{{7 \times 8}} = 3\,{\text{days}}$$

q: Two pipes, P and Q can fill a cistern in 12 and 15 minutes respectively. Both are opened together, but at the end of 3 minutes, P is turned off. In how many more minutes will Q fill the cistern?
s: P can fill cistern in 12 minutes P fills cistern in 1 minute = $$\frac{1}{{12}}$$ Q can fill cistern in 15 minutes Q fills cistern in 1 minute = $$\frac{1}{{15}}$$ part P and Q together can fill cistern in 1 minute, $$= \frac{1}{{12}} + \frac{1}{{15}} \Rightarrow \frac{9}{{60}}$$ part So, they can together fill cistern in 3 minute, $$= 3 \times \frac{9}{{60}} \Rightarrow \frac{9}{{20}}$$ part Rest Cistern = $$1 - \frac{9}{{20}}$$ = $$\frac{{11}}{{20}}$$ part $$\frac{{11}}{{20}}$$ part cistern must be filled by Q in $$\frac{{\frac{{11}}{{20}}}}{{\frac{1}{{15}}}} = 8\frac{1}{4}$$ minutes Alternatively, Pipe P can fill cistern in one minute = $$\frac{{100}}{{12}}$$ = 8.33% Pipe Q can fill cistern in one minute = $$\frac{{100}}{{15}}$$ = 6.66% (P + Q) together can fill the cistern in one minute = 15%; In 3 minutes cistern is filled = 45% P become off, then rest of cistern will be filled by Pipe Q in = $$\frac{{55}}{{6.66}}$$ = $$8\frac{1}{4}$$ minutes.

q: Two pipes can fill an empty tank separately in 24 minutes and 40 minutes respectively and a third pipe can empty 30 gallons of water per minute. If all three pipes are open, empty tanks become full in one hour. The capacity of the tank (in gallons) is:
s: Let capacity of the tank = x gallons; Part of the tank filled in 1 minute $$\begin{aligned} & = {\frac{x}{{24}}} + {\frac{x}{{40}}} - 30 \\ & {\text{Or}}, {\frac{x}{{24}}} + {\frac{x}{{40}}} - 30 = \frac{x}{{60}} \\ & {\text{Or}}, \frac{x}{{24}} + \frac{x}{{40}} - \frac{x}{{60}} = 30 \\ & {\text{Or}}, {\frac{{ {10x + 6x - 4x} }}{{240}}} = 30 \\ & {\text{Or}},\,12x = 30 \times 240 \\ & {\text{Or}},\,x = 600\,{\text{gallons}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A cistern can be filled by two pipes in 20 and 30 minutes respectively. Both pipes being opened, when the first pipe must be turned off so that the cistern may be filled in 10 minutes more.
s: % Cistern is filled by 1 st pipe in one minute = $$\frac{{100}}{{20}}$$ = 5% % Cistern is filled by 2 nd pipe in one minute = $$\frac{{100}}{{30}}$$ = 3.33% % cistern filled by 1 st and 2 nd pipes in one minute = 8.33% According to question, Cistern is totally filled by 2 nd pipe in last 10 minute. That means 2 nd pipe filled 33.3% of the cistern in last 10 minute and 66.66% of cistern is filled by 1 st and 2 nd pipe together in = $$\frac{{66.66}}{{8.33}}$$ = 8 minutes Thus, after 8 minute, 1 st pipe must be turned off.

q: A tank can be filled with water by two pipes A and B together in 36 minutes. If the pipe B was stopped after 30 minutes, the tank is filled in 40 minutes. The pipe B can alone fill the tank in:
s: Let the pipes fill the tank in x minutes. Part of tank filled by pipes A and B in one minute: $$\frac{1}{{36}}$$ Part of the tank filled by pipe A in 1 minute = $$\frac{1}{{36}} - \frac{1}{x}$$ According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & 30 \times \frac{1}{{\text{x}}} + 40 \left( {\frac{1}{{36}} - \frac{1}{{\text{x}}}} \right) = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{30}}{{\text{x}}} + \frac{{40}}{36} - \frac{{40}}{{\text{x}}} = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{30}}{{\text{x}}} + \frac{{10}}{9} - \frac{{40}}{{\text{x}}} = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{10}}{{\text{x}}} = \frac{1}{9} \end{aligned}$$ Hence, x = 90 minutes. Alternatively, % of tank filled by (A+B) in 1 minute = $$\frac{{100}}{{36}}$$ = 2.78% % of tank filled in 30 minutes = 2.78 × 30 = 83% That means 17% of tank can be filled by A in last 10 minutes Then, % tank filled by A in 1 minute = $$\frac{{17}}{{10}}$$ = 1.7% % of tank filled by B in 1 minute = 2.78 - 1.7 = 1.1% So, B alone can fill 100% tank in, = $$\frac{{100}}{{1.1}}$$ = 90 minutes (approx.)

q: A boy and a girl together fill a cistern with water. The boy pours 4 liters of water every 3 minutes and girl pours 3 litres every 4 minutes. How much time will it take to fill 100 litres of water in the cistern?
s: Water filled by (boy + girl) in one minute, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{4}{3} + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{{16 + 9}}{{12}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{25}}{{12}}\,{\text{liter}} \end{aligned}$$ Hence, time taken to fill 100 liter, $${\text{ = 100}} \times \frac{{12}}{{25}} = 48\,{\text{minutes}}$$

q: A tank has a leak which would empty the completely filled tank in 10 hours. If the tank is full of water and a tap is opened which admits 4 litres of water per minutes in the tank, the leak takes 15 hours to empty the tank. how many litres does the tank hold?
s: Let the capacity of the tank = q litres According to the question, Quantity of water emptied by the leak in 1 hour = $$\frac{\text{q}}{10}$$ litres Qunatity of water filled by the tap in 1 hour = 240 litres According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{{\text{q}}}{{10}} - \frac{{\text{q}}}{{15}} = 240 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{3{\text{q}} - 2{\text{q}}}}{{30}} = 240 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{9}{{30}} = 240 \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{q}} = 240 \times 30 \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{q}} = 7200\,{\text{litres}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A, B and C completed a work costing Rs. 1800. A work for 6 days, B for 4 days and C for 9 days. If their daily wages are in the ratio of 5 : 6 : 4, how much amount will be received by A?
s: Ratio of their daily wages = 5 : 6 : 4 Total wage = Rs. 1800 6 × 5x + 4 × 6x + 4 × 9x = 1800 [As A, B, C works for 6, 4, 9 days respectively] Or, 90x = 1800 Or, x = $$\frac{{1800}}{{90}}$$ Total amount of A = $$\frac{{1800 \times 30}}{{90}}$$ = Rs. 600

q: A man and a boy received Rs. 800 as wages for 5 days for the work they did together. The man's efficiency in the work was thrice times that of the boy. What are the daily wages of the boy?
s: Man = 3 boy Daily wages for them = $$\frac{{800}}{5}$$ = 160 4 boy (1 man + 1 boy) = 160 4 boy = 160 Or, boy = Rs. 40

q: Subhash can copy 50 pages in 10 hours; Subhash and Prakash together can copy 300 pages in 40 hours. In how much time can Prakash copy 30 pages?
s: Number of page copied by (Subhash + Prakash) in 1 hour = $$\frac{{300}}{{40}}$$ = 7.5 pages; Subhash copied pages in one hour = $$\frac{{50}}{{10}}$$ = 5 pages Hence, Prakash copied pages in one hour = 7.5 - 5 = 2.5 Thus, Prakash can copied 30 pages in = $$\frac{{30}}{{2.5}}$$ = 12 hour

q: An engineer undertakes a project to build a road 15 km long in 300 days and employs 45 men for the purpose. After 100 days, he finds 2.5 km of the road has been completed. Find the (approx.) number of extra men he must employ to finish the work in time.
s: Variation Method: In 100 days only 2.5 km road i.e. 16.66 % of work has been completed Men Days Road (km) 45 100↓ 2.5 x↑ 200 12.5↑ Arrows show the directions of variation of quantity with respect to each other $$\frac{{\text{x}}}{{45}} = \frac{{100 \times 12.5}}{{200 \times 2.5}}$$ x = 113 men; Required men to be increased, = 113 - 45 = 68

q: There is provision of food in fort for 1200 soldiers for 60 days. After 15 days, 200 soldiers leave the fort. Remaining food will last for how many days?
s: Work equivalence method: 1200 × 45 = 1000 × x Hence, x = 54 days Variation Method: After 15 days 200 soldiers leaved. Soldiers Food for days 1200 ↓ 45 1000 ↑ x (let) Arrows show the opposite variation to each other $$\frac{{1200}}{{1000}} = \frac{{\text{x}}}{{45}}$$ Or, x = $$\frac{{1200 \times 45}}{{1000}}$$ = 54 days.

q: A and B working together completed a job in 5 days. If A works twice as efficiently as he actually did and B works $$\frac{1}{3}$$ of actual efficiency, the work would have completed in 3 days. Find the for A to complete the job alone.
s: One Day's work of A and B together, $$\frac{1}{{\text{A}}} + \frac{1}{{\text{B}}} = \frac{1}{5}\,........({\text{i}})$$ When A works with twice efficiency,Then, $$\frac{2}{{\text{A}}} + \frac{1}{{3{\text{B}}}} = \frac{1}{3}\,........({\text{ii}})$$ on solving equations (i) and (ii), we get $$A = \frac{{25}}{4} = 6\frac{1}{4}$$

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 12 min and 16 min respectively. Both the pipes are opened together for a certain time but due to some obstruction the flow of water was restricted to $$\frac{7}{8}$$ of full flow in pipe A and $$\frac{5}{6}$$ of full in pipe B. This obstruction is removed after some time and tank is now filled in 3 min from that moment. How long was it before the full flow.
s: Let the obstruction remain for x min. Hence, Part of cistern filled in X min + part of cistern filled in 3 min = full cistern $$\left[ {\frac{{7{\text{x}}}}{{8 \times 12}} + \frac{{5{\text{x}}}}{{6 \times 16}}} \right]$$ $$+$$ $$\left[ {\frac{3}{{12}} + \frac{3}{{16}}} \right]$$ = 1 $$\frac{{12{\text{x}}}}{{96}} + \frac{7}{{16}} = 1$$ Thus, X = 4.5 min.

q: Three pipes A,B and C attached to a cistern. A can fill it in 10 min, B in 15 min, C is a waste pipe for emptying it. After opening both the pipes A and B, a man leaves the cistern and returns when the cistern should have been just full. Finding, however, that the waste pipe had left open, he closes it and the cistern now gets filled in 2 min. In how much time the pipe C, if opened alone, empty the full cistern?
s: Let pipe C alone can empty the cistern in x min. A fills cistern in 1 min = $$\frac{1}{{10}}$$ B fills cistern in 1 min = $$\frac{1}{{15}}$$ A and B together fill in 1 min $$= \frac{{10 \times 15}}{{10 + 15}} = \frac{{150}}{{25}} = 6\,{\text{min}}$$ Since, waste pipe was left open for 6 min then, 6 min, $$\frac{6}{x}$$ part of cistern will be emptied by C Now, $$\frac{6}{x}$$ part of the cistern would be filled by A and B in 2 min. Hence, cistern will be filled in $$\frac{3}{x}$$ min. And $$\frac{x}{3}$$ = 6 x = 18 min.

q: There is a group of 5 boys and 2 girls. The two groups working together can do four times as much work as a boy and a girl. Ratio of working capacities of a boy and a girl is:
s: Let 1 boy's 1 day's work = x And 1 girl's 1 day's work = y Now, (5 boys + 2 girls)'s work = 5x + 2y Given , 5x + 2y is equal to 4 times work done by a boy and a girl Thus, 5x + 2y = 4(x + y) 5x + 2y = 4x + 4y x = 2y $$\frac{{\text{x}}}{{\text{y}}} = \frac{2}{1}$$ Hence, the required ratio is 2 : 1

q: A group of 12 men can do a piece of work in 14 days and other group of 12 women can do the same work in 21 days. They begin together but 3 days before the completion of work, man's group leaves off. The total number of days to complete the work is:
s: Let x be the required number of days Given,12 men and 12 women can complete a work separately in 14 days and 21 days respectively Then, 12 men's 1 day work = $$\frac{1}{{14}}$$ And, 12 women's 1 day work = $$\frac{1}{{21}}$$ Then ,12 women's 3 days work = $$\frac{3}{{21}}$$ = $$\frac{1}{7}$$ The remaining work = $$1 - \frac{1}{7}$$ = $$\frac{6}{7}$$ Man's group leaves 3 days before the completion of work That is, they were working together for x - 3 days Thus, we have $$\frac{1}{7}$$ work left to be done in last 3 days by the women's group. This also means $$\frac{6}{7}$$ th of work has been done by both the groups (before men left) Now, (12 men + 12 women)'s 1 day work = $$\frac{1}{{14}} + \frac{1}{{21}}$$ = $$\frac{5}{{42}}$$ i.e., $$\frac{5}{{42}}$$ work is done by 2 groups in 1 day. So, $$\frac{6}{7}$$ of work is done by 2 groups together in $$\frac{{42}}{5} \times \frac{6}{7}$$ = $$\frac{{36}}{5}$$ days Total time take to complete the work will be = $$\frac{{36}}{5}$$ + 3 = $$\frac{{51}}{5}$$

q: Vimal can do a piece of work in 20 days, Vimal and Kamal together can do in 12 days. If Kamal does the work only for half a day daily then in how many days the work will be completed ?
s: Vimal's 1 day work = $$\frac{1}{{20}}$$ Since, Vimal and Kamal can together complete in 12 days i.e. (Vimal + Kamal)'s 1 day work = $$\frac{1}{{12}}$$ Then, Kamal's 1 day work, $$= \frac{1}{{12}} - \frac{1}{{20}} \Rightarrow \frac{2}{{60}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{30}}$$ If Kamal Works only for half a day daily, then his 1 day work becomes $$\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{{30}}$$ = $$\frac{1}{{60}}$$ Therefore, 1 day work of both Vimal and Kamal, $$= \frac{1}{{20}} + \frac{1}{{60}} \Rightarrow \frac{4}{{60}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{15}}$$ Hence, the work will be completed in 15 days.

q: There are three boats A, B and C, working together they carry 60 people in each trip. One day an early morning A carried 50 people in few trips alone. When it stopped carrying the passengers B and C started carrying the people together. It took a total of 10 trips to carry 300 people by A, B and C. It is known that each day on an average 300 people cross the river using only one of the 3 boats A, B and C. How many trips it would take to A to carry 150 passengers alone?
s: Combined efficiency of all the three boats = 60 passengers /trip Now, consider option (A) 15 trips and 150 passengers means efficiency of A = 10 passengers per trip A's efficiency = 10 passengers per trip Then, (B + C) combined efficiency = 50 passengers per trip Since, combined efficiency is 60 so option (A) is correct

q: Raj can do a piece of work in 20 days. He started the work and left after some days, when 25% work was done. After it Abhijit joined and completed it working for 10 days. In how many days Raj and Abhijit can do the complete work, working together?
s: Efficiency of Raj = $$\frac{{100}}{{20}}$$ = 5% Work completed by Raj = 25% Rest work = 75% Efficiency of Abhijit = $$\frac{{75}}{{10}}$$ = 7.5% Combined efficiency = 5 + 7.5 = 12.5% They will complete the whole work by working together in,= $$\frac{{100}}{{12.5}}$$ = 8 days

q: If 10 persons can do a job in 20 days, then 20 person with twice the efficiency can do the same job in:
s: By work equivalence method, man × days × work = MAN × DAYS × WORK 10 × 20 × 1 = 20 × 2 × x → x = 5 days

q: There was a leakage in the container of the refined oil. If 11 kg oil is leaked out per day then it would have lasted for 50 days, if the leakage was 15 kg per day, then it would have lasted for only 45 days. For how many days would the oil have lasted, if there was no leakage ant it was completely used for eating purpose?
s: Let x kg of oil be used for the eating purpose, daily, then (x + 11) × 50 = (x +15) × 45 → x = 25 Thus, Total quantity of oil, = (25 +11) × 50 = 1800 Hence, required number of days, = $$\frac{{1800}}{{25}}$$ = 72 days

q: If 2 men or 3 women or 4 boys can do a piece of work in 52 days, then the same piece of work will be done by 1 man, 1 woman and 1 boy in:

q: If one pipe A can fill a tank in 20 minutes, then 5 pipes, each of 20% efficiency of A, can fill the tank in:

q: X takes 4 days to complete one-third of a job. Y takes 3 days to complete one-sixth of the job and Z takes 5 days to complete half the job. If all of them work together for 3 days and X and Z quit, how long will it take for Y to complete the remaining work done.

q: Two typist of varying skills can do a job in 6 minutes if they work together. q: A and B completed a work together in 5 days. had A worked at twice the speed and B at half the speed, it would have taken them four days to complete the job. How much time would it take for A alone to do the work?

q: Two forest officials in their respective division were involved in the harvesting of tendu leave. q: Ram Lal is a renowned packager of fruits in Varanasi. He packs 70 mangoes or 56 guavas every day working 7 hours a day. His wife also helps him. q: A group of men decided to do a job in 4 days. But since 20 men dropped out every day, the job completed at the end of the 7 th day. How many men were there at the beginning?

q: Two persons having different productivity of labour, working together can reap a field in 2 days. If one-third of the field was reaped by the first man and rest by the other one working alternatively took 4 days. How long did it take for the faster person to reap the whole field working alone?

q: A group of workers was put on a job. From second day onwards, one worker was withdrawn each day. The job was finished when the last worker was withdrawn. Had no worker been withdrawn at any stage, the group would have finished the job in 55% of the time. How many workers were there in the group?

Sum of AP = {No. of terms (first term + last term)/2}] X = 10 workers.

q: A single reservoir supplies the petrol to the whole city, while the reservoir is fed by a single pipeline filling the reservoir with the stream of uniform volume. q: A is thrice good a workman as B and therefore is able to finish a job in 40 days less than B. Working together they can do it in:

q: A and B can compete a piece of work in 18 days. They worked together for 12 days and then A left. B alone finished the work in 15 days. If Rs. 1500 be paid for the work then A's share is:

q: If 3 men or 4 women can plough a field in 43 days, how long will 7 men and 5 women take to plough it?
s: 3 men or 4 women can plough the field in 43 days 3 men = 4 women 1 man = $$\frac{4}{3}$$ women 7 man = $$\frac{{28}}{3}$$ women 7 men and 5 women = $$5 + \frac{{28}}{3}$$ = $$\frac{{43}}{3}$$ women 4 women can plough field in 43 days So, 1 women can plough in = 43 × 4 days Hence, $$\frac{{43}}{3}$$ women can plough = $$\frac{{43 \times 4 \times 3}}{{43}}$$ = 12 days

q: To complete a piece of work A and B take 8 days, B and C 12 days. A, B and C take 6 days. A and C will take :
s: Given (A+B)'s one day's work = $$\frac{1}{8}$$ (B + C)'s one day's work = $$\frac{1}{{12}}$$ (A + B + C) 's 1 day's work = $$\frac{1}{6}$$ Work done by A, alone= (A + B + C) 's 1 day's work - (B + C)'s one day's work $$= \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{{12}} = \frac{{2 - 1}}{{12}} = \frac{1}{{12}}$$ Work done by C, alone = (A + B + C) 's 1 day's work - (A + B)'s one day’s work $$= \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{{4 - 3}}{{24}} = \frac{1}{{24}}$$ ⇒ (A + C)’s one day’s work $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{{12}} + \frac{1}{{24}} \\ & = \frac{{2 + 1}}{{24}} \\ & = \frac{3}{{24}} = \frac{1}{8} \end{aligned}$$ ⇒ (A + C) will take 8 days to complete the work together

q: Two pipes can fill the cistern in 10hr and 12 hr respectively, while the third empty it in 20hr. If all pipes are opened simultaneously, then the cistern will be filled in:

q: Three taps A, B and C together can fill an empty cistern in 10 minutes. The tap A alone can fill it in 30 minutes and the tap B alone in 40 minutes. How long will the tap C alone take to fill it?
s: A, B and C together can fill 100% empty tank in 10 minutes Work rate of (A + B + C) = $$\frac{{100}}{{10}}$$ = 10% per minute A alone can fill the tank in 30 minutes Work rate of A = $$\frac{{100}}{{30}}$$ = 3.33% per minute B alone can fill the tank in 40 minutes Work rate of B = $$\frac{{100}}{{40}}$$ = 2.5% Work rate of (A + B) = 3.33 + 2.5 = 5.83% per minute Work rate of C, = Work rate of (A + B + C) - (A + B) = 10 - 5.83 = 4.17% per minute So, C takes = $$\frac{{100}}{{4.17}}$$ ≈ 24 minutes to fill the tank

q: A and B working separately can do a piece of work in 9 and 15 days respectively. If they work for a day alternately, with A beginning, then the work will be completed in:

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 36 min. and 45 min. respectively. Another pipe C can empty the tank in 30 min. First A and B are opened. After 7 minutes, C is also opened. The tank filled up in:
s: Pipe A can fill empty tank in 36 min. Pipe A can fill the tank = $$\frac{{100}}{{36}}$$ = 2.77% per minute Pipe B can fill empty tank in 45 min. Pipe B can fill the tank = $$\frac{{100}}{{45}}$$ = 2.22% per min. A and B can together fill the tank = (2.77 + 2.22) ≈ 5% per minute So, A and B can fill the tank in 7 min. = 7 × 5 = 35% of the tank Rest tank to be filled = 100 - 35 = 65% C can empty the full tank in 30 min. C can empty the tank = $$\frac{{100}}{{30}}$$ = 3.33% per min. C is doing negative work i.e. emptying the tank A, B and C can together fill the tank, = 2.77% + 2.22% - 3.33% = 1.67% tank per minute So, A, B and C will take time to fill 65% empty tank, = $$\frac{{65}}{{1.67}}$$ = 39 min. (Approx)

q: Three men A, B, C working together can do a job in 6 hours less time than A alone, in one hour less time than B alone and in one half the time needed by C when working alone. Then A and B together can do the job in:
s: Time taken by A =x hours. Therefore taken by A, B and C together = (x - 6) Time taken by B = (x - 5) Time taken by C = 2(x - 6) Now, rate of work of A + Rate of work of B + Rate of work of C = Rate of work of ABC. $$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{{x - 5}} + \frac{1}{{2\left( {x - 6} \right)}} = \frac{1}{{x - 6}}$$ On solving above equation, we get x = 3, $$\frac{{40}}{6}$$ When x = 3, the expression (x - 6) becomes negative, thus it's not possible. $$\Rightarrow x = \frac{{40}}{6}$$ Time taken by A & B together = $$\frac{1}{{\frac{3}{{20}} + \frac{3}{5}}}$$ = $$\frac{4}{3}$$ hours

q: A does half as much work as B in one -sixth of the time.If together they take 10 days to complete a work, how much time shall B take to do it alone?
s: To do half of the work in one sixth of the time means A is 3 times as efficient as B. To understand this point just think if same work would have been done in one sixth of the time then A would have been six times as efficient as B. Now they together complete the work in 10 days. B is working with someone who is 3 times as efficient as himself. That means 4 people of B's efficiency finished the work in 10 days. So B alone would have done it in 40 days. A alone would have taken one third of this time. Alternatively, Given, $${\text{A}} \times \frac{1}{6} = {\text{B}} \times \frac{1}{2}$$ So, A = 3B Now, Given they together complete the work in 10 days So, One Day''s work of, (A + B) = $$\frac{{100}}{{10}}$$ = 10% (3B + B) = 10% 4B = 10% So, one day work of B = $$\frac{{10}}{4}$$ = 2.5% So, B can complete 100% work in = $$\frac{100}{2.5}$$ = 40 days

q: An employee pays Rs. 26 for each day a worker and forfeits Rs. 7 for each day he idle. At the end of 56 days, if the worker got Rs. 829, for how many days did the worker remain idle?
s: His Per day pay = Rs. 26 Total pay employee got = Rs. 829 Total pay he gets if he did not remain idle a single day, = 26 × 56 = Rs.1456 He Forfeits or fined = 1456 - 829 = Rs. 627 Per day he Forfeits Rs. 7 Means per idle day he loses = 26 + 7 = Rs. 33 So, Total idle days = $$\frac{{627}}{{33}}$$ = 19 days Alternatively, Let he works for X days and remain idle for (56 - X) Now, According to question, X × 26 - 7 × (56 - X) = 829 26X + 7X - 392 = 829 33X = 829 + 392 = 1221 X = 37 days Number of days remain idle = 56 -37 =19 days

q: A is 60% more efficient than B. In how many days will A and B working together complete a piece of work which A alone takes 15 days to finish?
s: Given, A is 60% more efficient of B Means, $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{A}} = {\text{B}} + 60\% \,{\text{of B}} \\ & {\text{A}} = {\text{B}} + \frac{{60{\text{B}}}}{{100}} \\ & {\text{A}} = \frac{{100{\text{B}} + 60{\text{B}}}}{{100}} \\ & {\text{A}} = \frac{{160{\text{B}}}}{{100}} \\ & {\text{A}} = \frac{{8{\text{B}}}}{5} \end{aligned}$$ A can complete whole work in 15 days. So, One day work of A = $$\frac{1}{{15}}$$ One day work of A = $$\frac{{8{\text{B}}}}{5}$$ = $$\frac{1}{{15}}$$ One day work of B = $$\frac{5}{{120}}$$ = $$\frac{1}{{24}}$$ One day work, (A + B) = $$\frac{1}{{15}} + \frac{1}{{24}}$$ One day work, (A + B) = $$\frac{{24 + 15}}{{360}}$$ = $$\frac{{39}}{{360}}$$ So, Time taken to finish the work by A and B together = $$\frac{{360}}{{39}}$$ = $$\frac{{120}}{{13}}$$ days Alternatively We can solve it through percentage method Given, A = $$\frac{{8{\text{B}}}}{5}$$ A can complete whole work in 15 days Work rate of A = $$\frac{{100}}{{15}}$$ = 6.66% per day Work rate of $$\frac{{8{\text{B}}}}{5}$$ = 6.66% Work rate of B = 4.16% per day Work rate of (A + B) = 6.66 + 4.16 = 10.82% per day So, A and B can complete 100% work in $$\frac{{120}}{{13}}$$ days

q: A pipe can fill a tank in 0.9 hours and another pipe can empty in 0.7 hours. If tank is completely filled and both pipes are opened simultaneously then 450 liters of water is removed from the tank is 2.5 hours. What is the capacity of the tank?
s: Pipe A can fill the empty tank in = 0.9 hours So work rate of the Pipe A = $$\frac{{100}}{{0.9}}$$ % per hour Pipe B can empty the tank in = 0.7 hours Negative Work rate of B = $$\frac{{100}}{{0.7}}$$ % per hour. (B is removing water, so, taken as negative work) Tank fill per hour = $$\frac{{100}}{{0.7}} - \frac{{100}}{{0.9}}$$ = 31.75% per hour Time Taken to empty the tank = $$\frac{{100}}{{31.75}}$$ ≈ 3.15 hours So, Capacity of the tank = 3.15 × 180 = 567 liters

q: A can do a work in 15 days and B in 20 days. If they work on it together for 4 days, then the fraction of the work that is left is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{15}}; \\ & {\text{B's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{20}}; \\ & \left( {{\text{A + B}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{15}} + \frac{1}{{20}}} = \frac{7}{{60}} \\ & \left( {{\text{A + B}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{4}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{7}{{60}} \times 4} = \frac{7}{{15}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Remaining}}\,{\text{work}}\, = {1 - \frac{7}{{15}}} = \frac{8}{{15}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A can lay railway track between two given stations in 16 days and B can do the same job in 12 days. With help of C, they did the job in 4 days only. Then, C alone can do the job in:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {{\text{A + B + C}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{4} \\ & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{16}} \\ & {\text{B's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{12}} \\ & \therefore {\text{C's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = \frac{1}{4} - \left( {\frac{1}{{16}} + \frac{1}{{12}}} \right) = {\frac{1}{4} - \frac{7}{{48}}} = \frac{5}{{48}} \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{C}}\,\,{\text{alone}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{do}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{in}} \\ & \frac{{48}}{5} = 9\frac{3}{5}\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 20, 30 and 60 days respectively. In how many days can A do the work if he is assisted by B and C on every third day?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{2}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = {\frac{1}{{20}} \times 2} = \frac{1}{{10}} \\ & \left( {{\text{A + B + C}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{20}} + \frac{1}{{30}} + \frac{1}{{60}}} = \frac{6}{{60}} = \frac{1}{{10}} \\ & {\text{Work}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{3}}\,{\text{days}} = {\frac{1}{{10}} + \frac{1}{{10}}} = \frac{1}{5} \\ & {\text{Now}},\,\frac{1}{5}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{3}}\,{\text{days}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Whole}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{in}}\, \\ & {3 \times 5} = 15\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A is thrice as good as workman as B and therefore is able to finish a job in 60 days less than B. Working together, they can do it in:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Ratio}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{times}}\,{\text{taken}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{B = 1:3}} \\ & {\text{The}}\,{\text{time}}\,{\text{difference}}\,{\text{is}}\,\left( {{\text{3 - 1}}} \right)\,{\text{2}}\,{\text{days}} \\ & {\text{while}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{take}}\,{\text{3}}\,{\text{days}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{takes}}\,{\text{1 }}\,{\text{day}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{If}}\,{\text{difference}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{time}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{2}}\,{\text{ days,}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{takes}}\,{\text{3}}\,{\text{days}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{If}}\,{\text{difference}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{time}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{60}}\,{\text{days,}} \\ & {\text{B}}\,{\text{takes}}\,\left( {\frac{3}{2} \times 60} \right) = 90\,{\text{days}} \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{takes}}\,{\text{30}}\,{\text{days}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{do}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{30}} \\ & {\text{B's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{90}} \\ & \left( {{\text{A + B}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{30}} + \frac{1}{{90}}} = \frac{4}{{90}} = \frac{2}{{45}} \\ & \therefore {\text{A}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{together}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{do}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{in}}\, \\ & \frac{{45}}{2} = 22\frac{1}{2}\,{\text{days}}\, \end{aligned}$$

q: A alone can do a piece of work in 6 days and B alone in 8 days. A and B undertook to do it for Rs. 3200. With the help of C, they completed the work in 3 days. How much is to be paid to C?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{C's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = \frac{1}{3} - \left( {\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{8}} \right) \\ & = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{7}{{24}} \\ & = \frac{1}{{24}} \\ & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{wages:B's}}\,{\text{wages:C's}}\,{\text{wages}} \\ & = \frac{1}{6}:\frac{1}{8}:\frac{1}{{24}} \\ & = 4:3:1 \\ & \therefore {\text{C's}}\,{\text{share}}\,{\text{(for}}\,{\text{3}}\,{\text{days}}\,{\text{)}} \\ & = Rs.\,\left( {3 \times \frac{1}{{24}} \times 3200} \right) \\ & = Rs.\,400 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 6 men and 8 boys can do a piece of work in 10 days while 26 men and 48 boys can do the same in 2 days, the time taken by 15 men and 20 boys in doing the same type of work will be:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{man's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = x\,{\text{and}} \\ & 1\,{\text{boy's}}\,{\text{1day's}}\,{\text{work}} = y \\ & {\text{Then,}}\,6x + 8y = \frac{1}{{10}}\,{\text{and}}\, \\ & 26x + 48y = \frac{1}{2} \\ & {\text{Solving}}\,{\text{these}}\,{\text{two}}\,{\text{equations,}}\,{\text{we}}\,{\text{get}} \\ & x = \frac{1}{{100}}\,and\,y = \frac{1}{{200}} \\ & {\text{(15}}\,{\text{men}}\,{\text{ + 20}}\,{\text{boy)'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{{15}}{{100}} + \frac{{20}}{{200}}} = \frac{1}{4} \\ & \therefore {\text{15}}\,{\text{men}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{20}}\,{\text{boys}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{ do}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{4}}\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A can do a piece of work in 4 hours; B and C together can do it in 3 hours, while A and C together can do it in 2 hours. How long will B alone take to do it?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{4}; \\ & {\text{(B + C)'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{3}; \\ & {\text{(A + C)'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{2}. \\ & {\text{(A + B + C)'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{3}} = \frac{7}{{12}} \\ & {\text{B's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{7}{{12}} - \frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{{12}} \\ & \therefore {\text{B}}\,{\text{along}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{take}}\,{\text{12}}\,{\text{hours}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{do}}\ ,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A can do a certain work in the same time in which B and C together can do it. If A and B together could do it in 10 days and C alone in 50 days, then B alone could do it in:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {{\text{A + B}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{10}} \\ & {\text{C's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{50}} \\ & \left( {{\text{A + B + C}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{10}} + \frac{1}{{50}}} = \frac{6}{{50}} = \frac{3}{{25}}........\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = \left( {{\text{B + C}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}}\,........\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & {\text{From}}\,\left( {\text{i}} \right)\,{\text{and}}\,\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right){\text{,we}}\,{\text{get}}:2 \times \left( {{\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}}} \right) \\ & = \frac{3}{{25}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{3}{{50}} \\ & \therefore {\text{B's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}}\left( {\frac{1}{{10}} - \frac{3}{{50}}} \right) \\ & = \frac{2}{{50}} = \frac{1}{{25}} \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{B}}\,\,{\text{alone}}\,{\text{could}}\,{\text{do}}\,{\text{the }}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{25}}\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A does 80% of a work in 20 days. He then calls in B and they together finish the remaining work in 3 days. How long B alone would take to do the whole work?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Whole}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{in}} \\ & = {20 \times \frac{5}{4}} = 25\,{\text{days}} \\ & {\text{Now}},\,\left( {1 - \frac{4}{5}} \right)\,\,i.e., \\ & \ frac{1}{5}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{3}}\,{\text{days}} \\ & {\text{Whole}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{in}} \\ & = \left( {3 \times 5} \right) = 15\,{\text{days}} \\ & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{25}}, \\ & \left( {{\text{A + B}}} \right)\,{\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{15}} \\ & \therefore {\text{B's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{15}} - \frac{1}{{25}}} = \frac{4}{{150}} = \frac{2}{{75}} \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{B}}\,\,{\text{alone}}\,{\text{would}}\,{\text{do}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{in}} \\ & \frac{{75}}{2} = 37\frac{1}{2}\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A machine P can print one lakh books in 8 hours, machine Q can print the same number of books in 10 hours while machine R can print them in 12 hours. All the machines are started at 9 A.M. while machine P is closed at 11 A.M. and the remaining two machines complete work. Approximately at what time will the work (to print one lakh books) be finished ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {{\text{P + Q + R}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{{10}} + \frac{1}{{12}}} = \frac{{37}}{{120}} \\ & {\text{Work}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by} }\,{\text{P,}}\,{\text{Q}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{R}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{2}}\,{\text{hours}} \\ & = {\frac{{37}}{{120}} \times 2} = \frac{{37}}{{60}} \\ & {\text{Remaining}}\,{\text{work}} = {1 - \frac{{37}}{{60}}} = \frac{{23}}{{60}} \\ & \left( {{\text{Q + R}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{10}} + \frac{1}{{12}}} = \frac{{11}}{{60}} \\ & {\text{Now}},\frac{{11}}{{60}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\ text{by}}\,{\text{Q}}\,\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{R}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour}} \\ & {\text{So}},\frac{{23}}{{6 0}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{Q}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{R}}\,{\text{in }} \\ & = {\frac{{60}}{{11}} \times \frac{{23}}{{60}}} = \frac{{23}}{{11}}\,{\text{hours}} \approx 2\,{\text{hours}} \\ & {\text{So,}}{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{finished}}\,{\text{approximately}} \\ & {\text{2}}\,{\text{hours}}\,{\text{after}}\,{\text{11}}\,{\text{A}}{\text{.M}}{\text{.,}}\,{\text{i}}{\text{.e}}{\text{.,}}\, {\text{around}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{P}}{\text{.M}}{\text{.}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A can finish a work in 18 days and B can do the same work in 15 days. B worked for 10 days and left the job. In how many days, A alone can finish the remaining work?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{B's}}\,{\text{10}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{15}} \times 10} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & {\text{Remaining}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {1 - \frac{2}{3}} = \frac{1}{3} \\ & {\text{Now}},\frac {1}{{18}}{\text{work}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day}} \\ & \therefore \frac{1}{3}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{in}} \\ & {18 \times \frac{1}{3}} = 6\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: 4 men and 6 women can complete a work in 8 days, while 3 men and 7 women can complete it in 10 days. In how many days will 10 women complete it?
s: Let 1 man's 1 day's work = x and 1 woman's 1 day's work = y Then, 4x + 6y = $$\frac{1}{8}$$ and 3x + 7y = $$\frac{1}{{10}}$$ Solving the two equations, we get $$x = \frac{{11}}{{400}},\,\,\,y = \frac{1}{{400}}$$ ∴ 1 woman's 1 day's work = $$\frac{1}{{400}}$$ ⇒ 10 women's 1 day's work = $${\frac{1}{{400}} \times 10}$$ = $$\frac{1}{{40}}$$ Hence, 10 women will complete the work in 40 days

q: A and B can together finish a work 30 days. They worked together for 20 days and then B left. After another 20 days, A finished the remaining work. In how many days A alone can finish the work?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {{\text{A + B}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{20}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{30}} \times 20} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & {\text{Remaining}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {1 - \frac{2}{3}} = \frac{1}{3} \\ & {\text{Now}},\frac{1}{3}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{in }}\,{\text{20}}\,{\text{days}} \\ & \therefore {\text{The}}\,{\text{whole}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{be}}\, {\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{in}} \\ & {20 \times 3} = 60\,days \end{aligned}$$

q: P can complete a work in 12 days working 8 hours a day. Q can complete the same work in 8 days working 10 hours a day. If both P and Q work together, working 8 hours a day, in how many days can they complete the work?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{P}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{complete}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = \,\left( {12 \times 8} \right){\text{hrs}}{\text{.}} = 96\,{\text{hrs}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{Q}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{complete}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = \left( {8 \times 10} \right){\text{hrs}}{\text{.}} = 80\,{\text{hrs}}{\text{.}} \\ & \therefore {\text{P's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{96}}\,{\text{and}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Q's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{80}} \\ & \left( {{\text{P + Q}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{96}} + \frac{1}{{80}}} = \frac{{11}}{{480}} \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{both}}\,{\text{P}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{Q}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{finish}}\ ,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{{480}}{{11}}} {\text{ hrs}}{\text{.}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Number}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{days}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{8}}\,{\text{hours}}\,{\text{each}} \\ & {\frac{{480}}{{11}} \times \frac{1}{8}} = \frac{{60}}{{11}}{\text{days}} = 5\frac{5}{{11}}{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: 10 women can complete a work in 7 days and 10 children take 14 days to complete the work. How many days will 5 women and 10 children take to complete the work?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 1\,woman's\,1\,day's\,work = \frac{1}{{70}} \\ & {\text{1}}\,{\text{child's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{140}} \\ & \left( {{\text{5}}\,{\text{women + 10}}\,{\text{children}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{5}{{70}} + \frac{{10}}{{140}}} = {\frac{1}{{14}} + \frac{1}{{14}}} = \frac{1}{7} \\ & \therefore {\text{5}}\,{\text{women}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{10}}\,{\text{chidren}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{complete}} \\ & {\text{the}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{7}}\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: X and Y can do a piece of work in 20 days and 12 days respectively. X started the work alone and then after 4 days Y joined him till the completion of the work. How long did the work last?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{work}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{X}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{4}}\,{\text{days}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{20}} \times 4} = \frac{1}{5} \\ & {\text{Remaining}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {1 - \frac{1}{5}} = \frac{4}{5} \\ & \left( {{\text{X + Y}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{20}} + \frac{1}{{12}}} = \frac{8}{{60}} = \frac{2}{{15}} \\ & {\text{Now}},\frac{2}{{15}}{\text{work}}\,{ \text{is}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{X}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{Y}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day}}. \\ & {\ text{So}},\,\frac{4}{5}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{X}}\,{\text{and}}\,{ \text{Y}}\,{\text{in}} \\ & {\frac{{15}}{2} \times \frac{4}{5}} = 6\,{\text{days}} \\ & {\text{Hence,}}\,{\text{total}}\,{\text{time}}\,{\text{taken}} \\ & = \left( {6 + 4} \right)\,{\text{days}} \\ & = 10\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A is 30% more efficient than B. How much time will they, working together, take to complete a job which A alone could have done in 23 days?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Ratio}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{times}}\,{\text{taken}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{B}} \\ & = 100:130 = 10:13 \\ & {\text{Suppose}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{takes}}\,x\,{\text{days}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{do}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & {\text{Then}},10:13::23:x \\ & \Rightarrow x = {\frac{{23 \times 13}}{{10}}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{299}}{{10}} \\ & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{23}} \\ & {\text{B's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{{10}}{{299}} \\ & \left( {{\text{A + B}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{23}} + \frac{{10}}{{299}}} \\ & = \frac{{23}}{{299}} \\ & = \frac{1}{{13}} \\ & \therefore A\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{together}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{complete}} \\ & \,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{13}}\,{\text{days}}{\text{.}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Ravi and Kumar are working on an assignment. Ravi takes 6 hours to type 32 pages on a computer, while Kumar takes 5 hours to type 40 pages. How much time will they take, working together on two different computers to type an assignment of 110 pages?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Number}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{pages}}\,{\text{typed}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{Ravi}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour}} \\ & = \frac{{32}}{6} = \frac{{16}}{3} \\ & {\text{Number}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{ pages}}\,{\text{typed}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{Kumar}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour}} \\ & = \frac{{40}}{5} = 8 \\ & {\text{Number}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{pages}}\,{\text{typed}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{both}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{1}}\, {\text{hour}} \\ & = {\frac{{16}}{3} + 8} = \frac{{40}}{3} \\ & \therefore {\text{Time}}\,{\text{taken}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{both}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{type}}\,{\text{110}}\,{\text{pages}} \\ & = {110 \times \frac{3}{{40}}} {\text{hours}} \\ & = 8\frac{1}{4}\,{\text{hours}}\,{\text{(or)}}\,{\text{8}}\,{\text{hours}}\,{\text{15}}\,{\text{minutes}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A, B and C can complete a piece of work in 24, 6 and 12 days respectively. Working together, they will complete the same work in:
s: Formula: If A can do a piece of work in n days, then A's 1 day's work = $$\frac{1}{{\text{n}}}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & (A + B + C)'s\,1\,{\text{day's work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{24}} + \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{{12}}} = \frac{7}{{24}} \end{aligned}$$ Formula: If A's 1 day's work = $$\frac{1}{{\text{n}}}$$ , then A can finish the work in n days So, all the three together will complete the job in $${\frac{{24}}{7}} {\text{ days}} = 3\frac{3}{7}{\text{ days}}$$

q: Sakshi can do a piece of work in 20 days. Tanya is 25% more efficient than Sakshi. The number of days taken by Tanya to do the same piece of work is:
s: Ratio of times taken by Sakshi and Tanya = 125 : 100 = 5 : 4 Suppose Tanya takes x days to do the work 5 : 4 :: 20 : x ⇒ $$x = {\frac{{4 \times 20}}{5}}$$ ⇒ x = 16 days Hence, Tanya takes 16 days to complete the work

q: A takes twice as much time as B or thrice as much time as C to finish a piece of work. Working together, they can finish the work in 2 days. B can do the work alone in:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Suppose}}\,{\text{A,}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{C}}\,{\text{take}} \\ & x,\,\ frac{x}{2},\,\frac{x}{3}\,{\text{days}}\,{\text{respectively}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{finish}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & {\text{Then}},\, {\frac{1}{x} + \frac{2}{x} + \frac{3}{x}} = \frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{6}{x} = \frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 12 \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{takes}}\, {\frac{{12}}{2}} \\ & = 6\,{\text{days}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{finish}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{work}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A and B can complete a work in 15 days and 10 days respectively. They started doing the work together but after 2 days B had to leave and A alone completed the remaining work. The whole work was completed in :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {{\text{A + B}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{15}} + \frac{1}{{10}}} = \frac{1}{6} \\ & {\text{Work}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{2}}\,{\text{days}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{6} \times 2} = \frac{1}{3} \\ & {\text{Remaining}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {1 - \frac{1}{3}} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & {\text{Now}},\,\frac{1}{{15}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day}} \\ & \therefore \frac{2}{3}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{a}}\,{\text{in}} \\ & {15 \times \frac{2}{3}} = 10\,{\text{days}} \\ & {\text{Hence,}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{total}}\,{\text{time}}\,{\text{taken}} \\ & = {10 + 2} = 12\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A and B can do a piece of work in 30 days, while B and C can do the same work in 24 days and C and A in 20 days. They all work together for 10 days when B and C leave. How many days more will A take to finish the work?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{2(A + B + C)'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{30}} + \frac{1}{{24}} + \frac{1}{{20}}} \\ & = \frac{{15}}{{120}} = \frac{1}{8} \\ & \therefore \left( {{\text{A + B + C}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = \frac{1}{{2 \times 8}} = \frac{1}{{16}} \\ & {\text{Work}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A,}}\,{\text{B,}}\,{\text{C}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{10}}\,{\text{days}} \\ & = \frac{{10}}{{16}} = \frac{5}{8} \\ & {\text{Remaining}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {1 - \frac{5}{8}} = \frac{3}{8} \\ & {\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{16}} - \frac{1}{{24}}} = \frac{1}{{48}} \\ & {\text{Now}},\,\frac{1}{{48}}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{isdone}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{in}}\ ,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day}} \\ & {\text{So}},\,\frac{3}{8}\,{\text{work}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{done}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{in}} \\ & {48 \times \frac{3}{8}} = 18\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A works twice as fast as B. If B can complete a work in 12 days independently, the number of days in which A and B can together finish the work in :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Ration}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{rates}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{working}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{ A}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{B}} \\ & = 2:1 \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{ratio}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{times}}\,{\text{taken}} = 1:2 \\ & {\text{B's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} = \frac{1}{{12}} \\ & \therefore {\text{A's}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = \frac{1}{3};\,({\text{2 times}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{B's}}\,{\text{work}}) \\ & \left( {{\text{A + B}}} \right){\text{'s}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{day's}}\,{\text{work}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{{12}}} = \frac{3}{{12}} = \frac{1}{4} \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{B}}\,{\text{together}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{finish}}\,{\text{the}} \\ & {\text{work}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{4}}\,{\text{days}}{\text{.}}\, \end{aligned}$$

q: Twenty women can do a work in sixteen days. Sixteen men can complete the same work in fifteen days. What is the ratio between the capacity of a man and a woman?

q: A and B can do a work in 8 days, B and C can do the same work in 12 days. A, B and C together can finish it in 6 days. A and C together will do it in :

q: A can finish a work in 24 days, B in 9 days and C in 12 days. B and C start the work but are forced to leave after 3 days. The remaining work was done by A in:

q: X can do a piece of work in 40 days. He works at it for 8 days and then Y finished it in 16 days. How long will they together take to complete the work?

q: A and B together can do a piece of work in 30 days. A having worked for 16 days, B finishes the remaining work alone in 44 days. In how many days shall B finish the whole work alone?

q: Ayesha can complete a piece of work in 16 days. Amita can complete the same piece of work in 8 days. If both of them work together in how many days can they complete the same piece of work ?
s: Ayesha's 1 day's work $$= \frac{1}{{16}}$$ Amita's 1 day's work $$= \frac{1}{{8}}$$ (Ayesha + Amitha)'s 1 day's work $$\begin{aligned} & = {\frac{1}{{16}} + \frac{1}{8}} \\ & = \frac{3}{{16}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Both together can complete the work in $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{16}}{3} \\ & = 5\frac{1}{3}{\text{ days}} \end{aligned}$$
